 11/19 Preview – Zuccarello, Fiala Beginning to Thrive + Moore Out, Helenius in, Gustafsson’s Strong Return, Coaching Reunion
 By Zach Dooley 
 6 hours ago 
 320 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (6-11-2) @ Toronto Maple Leafs (8-13-2)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 20/84
 WHEN: Thursday, November 19 @ 4:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Scotiabank Arena – Toronto, ONT
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: The Kings continue on a four-game roadtrip, as they visit the Toronto Maple Leafs, with hopes of building on Tuesday’s win over Boston. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Forward Quinton Byfield led the Kings last season with three goals in two games played against the Maple Leafs, including the overtime game-winning goal in both victories over Toronto. Forward Adrian Kempe led the team with five points (2-3-5) across the pair of games, while forward Alex Laferriere also found the back of the net twice in two games versus Toronto. 
 KINGS VITALS: The Kings held a full-team morning skate today at Scotiabank Arena, in advance of tonight’s game with the Maple Leafs. 
 Coming off a shutout victory over Boston on Tuesday, goaltender Darcy Kuemper will make his second consecutive start tonight in Toronto. Kuemper has a lifetime record of 5-5-0 versus the Maple Leafs, with a .865 save percentage and a 3.31 goals-against average. 
 Here is a projected lineup for tonight’s game, based on today’s full-team morning skate –
 Turcotte – Laferriere – Kempe
Fiala – Byfield – Zuccarello
Laughton – Haula – Armia
Lee – Helenius – Perry
 Gustafsson – Clarke
Edmundson – Doughty
Anderson – Dumoulin
 Kuemper
Forsberg
 Forward Trevor Moore is not expected to play tonight, out “day-to-day” per Peter Laviolette, with forward Samuel Helenius checking in. Forward Artemi Panarin is not expected back in the lineup tonight, his third game away for personal reasons. Defenseman Cody Ceci is tonight’s projected scratch. 
 MAPLE LEAFS VITALS: Toronto is on a seven-game losing streak entering tonight’s action, extended with a 6-3 defeat in Chicago on Tuesday evening. 
 Per David Alter of The Hockey News, here’s how the Maple Leafs lined up last time out against the Blackhawks –
 Leafs lines during warmups @ CHI Nov. 17/26 Cowan-Matthews-Roslovic Tverberg-Tavares-Nylander McKenna-Paul-Joshua Duhaime-Blueger-MacEwen McCabe-Raddysh Rielly-Stecher OEL-Tanev Bobrovsky (starter) Stolarz @Ozoon_CA https://t.co/IVjNp7SOJ2
 — David Alter (@davidalter) November 18, 2026 
 Forward Auston Matthews is one of eight players around the NHL with 30+ points this season, as he leads his team in goals (12), assists (18) and points (30). Forward John Tavares led the way for the Maple Leafs last season with three goals and five points in the two head-to-head matchups against the Kings. 
 Storyline Of The Day – 
Goals in back-to-back games here for forward Mats Zuccarello.
 Zuccarello said after the win over Boston that he’s starting to feel like himself out there again. He’s starting to look like it, for sure. Zuccarello has always been a productive offensive player, even deep into his career. I think that he’s the kind of guy who really needs to play with other players of that ilk. He’s finally got that line with Kevin Fiala back from injury. Along with Quinton Byfield, that’s the second scoring line the Kings have lacked all season long. 
 “Definitely it looks that way to me, you can tell that he’s involved, he’s moving, the puck is on his stick, he’s making plays, he’s putting pucks at the net,” Laviolette said of Zuccarello. “It’s a real bonus for us.”
 As they’ve played together, Zuccarello feels the line is beginning to build a bit more chemistry. 
 Zuccarello and Fiala are close on a personal level, from their time in Minnesota, but while they played together often on the power play, it was rarely a pairing used 5-on-5. With a Panarin/Kempe pairing established on the top line, trying to put those two players together on another scoring line was the idea coming in. Injuries have prevented that for the bulk of the season, but both players are healthy now and both players look like themselves. 
 “I haven’t been up to my game in terms of my injuries and my body-wise, so I’m starting to feel a little bit better,” Zuccarello added. “Kev has been out for a long time, so the fact that he’s back is really nice for our team. I can see it in him every day, getting more confidence, making plays and hopefully we can keep building that chemistry and contribute a little bit more to the team.”
 As Fiala returns to action, we’re starting to see him come into form as well.
 It’s small moments within the game, really. The shifty, little moves to show that Fiala still has the edges where they need to be and the agility where it needs to be. That’s always been his game and now that he’s gotten a few in the bank, I think it’s still there. For Fiala’s part, he feels like he’s in a good place and feels like he’s continuing to improve, both individually and within his line with Zuccarello and Byfield.
 “I do think last game was better, so that’s nice,” Fiala said of his process. “As the games go on, practices, all of that, I’m getting into the flow more and more. I think, still, there are steps to take, missing nine months, it’s not going to be a week or two, it’s going to take some time. I’m trying my best to get back as quick as possible at my top game again.”
 You worry a little bit when a player comes back about this stretch upcoming. The adrenaline is pumping for your return. Getting back on the road for the first time, same thing. But now it’s just routine. That’s the time to maybe monitor it. 
 That’s more narrative than anything, though. 
 Especially with Panarin out, the Kings need that line to deliver. They got that on Tuesday. It’s a line that has the ability to help drive a team that struggles to score offensively. 
 “They haven’t played a ton of games, but I think with Zucc coming off a limited amount of time off and Kevin coming off a substantial amount of time off, I think it’s going to take a little bit for those guys to continue to work up to speed, but I do think that they were noticeable [in Boston],” Laviolette added. “They possessed the puck, they created chances, they scored a goal, they had a lot of opportunities. They were probably our most effective line offensively.”
 Now they need to get it again tonight.
 3 To Watch For – 
– With the projected lineup above, there’s a little bit of guesswork on my part. 
 I did not see formal line rushes from the Kings and I think there are two likely ways we could see the lineup shake out. I think that we could see Laughton slide up with Haula and Armia, as it’s laid out above. I think that we could also see Andre Lee be the player sliding up, with Laughton shifting to the wing and Helenius taking the 4C role. Don’t have a ton of additional information beyond that. Moore is out on a day-to-day basis, per Laviolette, and Helenius will be in the lineup for sure. 
 Just when you thought that the lineup was trending towards full, another hit up front. Such is life. The Kings are without Panarin tonight and will now be without Moore as well. I felt that line was solid towards the end of the homestand and it’s a trusted line, with matchup ability. Lots of hard minutes, defensive-zone starts, penalty kill minutes. Could see Laughton being the ideal fit for those reasons, though Lee has played up in the lineup at times and I thought he had a good night in Boston. Different personnel, I could see it being Corey Perry, as it was when Zuccarello was out, but with the matchup nature, I think Laughton is the most likely fit. We’ll see.
 For tonight, though, the Kings are down two forwards in the Top-9 and we’ll see where both Panarin and Moore are at come Saturday’s game in Ottawa. 
 – Pretty strong return to action for defenseman Erik Gustafsson.
 A goal and an assist in the 3-0 Kings victory.
 As Boston pushed late in the game, they started to control the puck and the shot attempts more down the stretch, which tanked some numbers overall, but Gustafsson was again among the best. With him on the ice, the Kings controlled just shy of 60 percent of the shot attempts, as he ranked only behind his defensive partner, Brandt Clarke, among Kings blueliners. Looking even better were his scoring chance metrics, as the Kings outchanced the Bruins 9-4 with Gustafsson on the ice at 5-on-5, trailing only Zuccarello among all Los Angeles skaters. 4-1 in high-danger opportunities as well.
 I wrote in Tuesday’s pre-game preview that the biggest things Gustafsson brings for the Kings, that were missed at the end of the homestand, were his controlled zone exits and zone entries. Look at Zuccarello’s goal.
 Goals in back-to-back games for Zuc! https://t.co/UMI2P26IcN
 — LA Kings (@LAKings) November 18, 2026 
 It’s not the craziest play in the world. But Gustafsson takes the puck off a controlled zone exit by Clarke. He uses his skating to make a move in the neutral zone and he gains the offensive blueline with possession. His shot gets blocked but because of the space he created, with puck possession, it put the rebound in a dangerous area for Zuccarello to clean up. It’s those kinds of plays you notice with Gustafsson and you really value when he’s out of the lineup. It’s not a secret that it’s not a strength of the group overall, which becomes a problem – as it was last season – when Gustafsson is out. Nice to have him back in action and I thought that by all methods of evaluation, including the simply eye test, he was quite good. 
 – Lastly, the Kings will take on former Head Coach Jim Hiller for the first time since he was relieved of his duties by the organization back in February. 
 Hiller was hired as the Head Coach of the Maple Leafs over the summer and has led Toronto to an early-season record of 8-13.2. Hiller coached the Kings for parts of three seasons, beginning in February 2024, and totaled a regular-season record of 104-64-32, good for a .600 points percentage, the second best mark in franchise history. 
 “I see some familiar faces, they’re just a great organization, from top to bottom, great people and I really have some fond memories,” Hiller said this morning. “Not just the team, we had moderate success, you can argue that point, but the people, I have great relationships with the people there and it’s good to see them.”
 Nothing but class in that answer and for whatever you want to think about Jim Hiller, it was nice to see him today and he always showed me that level of respect with the Kings. On the ice, an old coach against his former team should only add to desperation you’d expect from both sides tonight.
 Kings and Maple Leafs, as a four-game roadtrip rolls on. The Kings will hope to do what they haven’t for the majority of this season and keep momentum rolling from Tuesday’s win over Boston. See what they can muster up tonight in Toronto.
